payload.title: 15 Engagement Ring Styles and Who Each One Suits
payload.excerpt: Solitaire, halo, toi et moi, east-west and 11 more engagement ring styles, each matched to personality, lifestyle, hand shape and a wedding abroad.
key_takeaways: Choose the overall style first and the setting that holds the stone second, because GIA treats the look of a ring and the way its stone is secured as two different things.
Halo, pavé and cluster designs rely on many small stones, so book a jeweller check every six months, or at least yearly.
When you don't know the wearer's hand well, a round or princess centre or a three-stone layout is the safest choice, as GIA says these suit almost any finger.

The 15 engagement ring styles in this guide are solitaire, halo, hidden halo, three-stone, toi et moi, east-west, cluster, vintage-inspired, art deco, pavé, bezel style, split shank, eternity-style, bypass and coloured gemstone centres.

faq.q: What are the different types of engagement rings?
faq.a: The main styles are solitaire, halo, hidden halo, three-stone, toi et moi, east-west, cluster, vintage-inspired, art deco, pavé, bezel style, split shank, eternity-style, bypass and coloured gemstone centres.

faq.q: What is the difference between an engagement ring style and a setting?
faq.a: The style is the overall arrangement of stones; the setting is how each stone is secured.

faq.q: Is a solitaire or a halo engagement ring better?
faq.a: Neither. A solitaire is clean and pairs easily with bands; a halo adds sparkle and size but needs more checks.

faq.q: What is the most flattering engagement ring style for my hand?
faq.a: GIA says round and princess centres and three-stone designs suit almost any finger, and simpler designs suit shorter fingers.

faq.q: Which engagement ring styles suit an active lifestyle?
faq.a: Bezel styles, as GIA calls them practical for active wearers, and low-profile designs, which snag less.

faq.q: Can you wear a coloured gemstone engagement ring every day?
faq.a: Yes, with the right stone: sapphire and ruby are 9 on the Mohs scale, while emerald needs a protective setting and more care.
